title: Async tool ACK multiplexing caused tenant correlation loss and misattributed function responses
creator: Amina Patel
description: Several customers using multiplexed streaming over the hosted API reported that function/tool responses were sometimes attributed to the wrong tenant or request. The misattribution happens intermittently under moderate concurrency and when upstream proxies retry or reorder ACK frames. Users observed: (1) a tool call response appearing in a different session, (2) structured JSON payloads merged with an adjacent response, and (3) downstream parsers failing due to mixed envelopes. This is a customer escalation affecting Hosted and some Dedicated customers using proxy-based multiplexing.
reproduction_steps: 1) Enable multiplexed async tool calls (streaming) with multiple tenants sharing a persistent connection. 2) Send concurrent tool-invoke requests that produce structured JSON outputs. 3) Introduce a proxy-induced retry/reorder on ACK frames (simulate transient 503 then retry). 4) Observe that response envelopes occasionally get swapped or merged; parser on client receives combined/misaligned JSON fragments.
investigation_summary: Root cause: in the async multiplexing code path we rely on a best-effort ACK->payload correlation window keyed by connection+sequence. Under proxy retries the server receives duplicate ACKs and a stale sequence is re-used before the previous payload has been fully flushed from the transmission queue. A race in the framing layer allows two payloads to be assigned to the same correlation token when the flush/ack lifecycle crosses a retry boundary. Additionally, the output framing delimiter used for function envelopes is not guaranteed unique when payloads contain unescaped control sequences, causing downstream parsers to conflate boundaries. Reproduced reliably with a test harness that injects ACK reorder and delays.
proposed_fix: 1) Change correlation token to include an increasing per-request nonce (not just sequence) that is validated against in-flight message set. 2) Harden framing by switching to length-prefixed envelopes for tool/function outputs (explicit size header) so payloads cannot be merged by delimiter collisions. 3) Add server-side dedup and acknowledgement fencing: ignore an ACK that references a correlation nonce that is no longer in flight. 4) Add a compatibility flag and rollout plan to avoid breaking older dedicated/private agents that expect delimiter framing.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): runtime-1.19+ with a feature flag enabled for 5% of hosted traffic; monitor misattribution metrics and parser error rates. Phase 2 (broader): enable for all hosted after 48h of stable metrics. Phase 3 (Dedicated/Private): provide a controlled minor release (1.19.1) and documentation for operators to opt in; default remains delimiter framing for 30 days to allow operator upgrades. All phases include a fallback that maps mismatched tool responses to a 'correlation_error' status and triggers a safe retry policy.
qa_tests: - Integration harness that simulates proxy reorders and verifies envelope uniqueness under high concurrency. - Regression test that sends payloads with embedded control chars and verifies length-prefixed parsing succeeds. - End-to-end customer scenario replay using captured production traces from affected customers. - Load test at 5k concurrent connections to validate no performance regression.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: tool_response_misattribution_count, framing_parse_errors, correlation_nonce_mismatch_rate. Add alert: framing_parse_errors > 5/min or tool_response_misattribution_count > 1 in 10 minutes (P0). Dashboards: Per-tenant time series showing misattribution events and retry correlation.
backfill_and_mitigation: Short-term mitigation deployed: server-side defensively rejects overlapping assignments and returns explicit correlation_error for suspicious ACKs (rollback safe). Support runbook created for Customer Support to map incidents to this ticket and advise temporary proxy config changes (disable simple retry-on-ACK, add jittered backoff).
